goal: a stranger can install the CLI, run it against their own data, and get a correct report without asking anyone for help
for_whom: someone who found the repo today and has never spoken to the maintainer
requirements: the documented install command works on a clean machine
the example in the README runs against the shipped sample data and prints a report
a wrong input produces a clear error instead of a traceback
the release page carries the same version the README names

checks.the documented install command works on: run the install line from the README in a fresh container and paste the output
checks.the example in the README runs against t: copy-paste the README example verbatim and compare its output to the sample report in docs/
checks.a wrong input produces a clear error ins: run the CLI against a malformed file and read the last line it prints
checks.the release page carries the same versio: compare the version string in the README with the tag on the newest release

out_of_scope: a hosted version of the tool
stop_rule: stop when all four are demonstrably true; hand back before changing anything a user's data depends on
first_action: run the README install line in a container and record exactly what it prints
ground_truth: the sample data is committed at examples/sample.csv and never regenerated
the version lives in one place: pyproject.toml
release tags are the only source of truth for what shipped
